title: Parable of the ten virgins part 1
scripture_text: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went to meet the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish, and five were wise. The five who were foolish didn’t take enough olive oil for their lamps, but the other five were wise enough to take along extra oil. When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep. “At midnight they were roused by the shout, ‘Look, the bridegroom is coming! Come out and meet him!’ “All the bridesmaids got up and prepared their lamps. Then the five foolish ones asked the others, ‘Please give us some of your oil because our lamps are going out.’ “But the others replied, ‘We don’t have enough for all of us. Go to a shop and buy some for yourselves.’ “But while they were gone to buy oil, the bridegroom came. Then those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was locked. Later, when the other five bridesmaids returned, they stood outside, calling, ‘Lord! Lord! Open the door for us!’ “But he called back, ‘Believe me, I don’t know you!’ “So you, too, must keep watch! For you do not know the day or hour of my return.’’
devotional:
One of the things that causes much debate and confusion among Christians is the Second coming of Christ. People form theological allegiances with others based on what they believe about Jesus’ return. Churches have split because there was no commonality when it came to what people believed about Jesus’ second coming. The return of Jesus has for many become a divisive and contentious topic, but this was never meant to be.

In the book of Matthew, we have five different sections of teaching given by Jesus. The last section of teaching that Matthew records for us is what is known as the Olivet Discourse. This is an extended teaching given by Christ about his second coming and the end of the world. This discourse is recorded in Matthew chapters 24 and 25. If you were to take the time to read through it you would notice that in a general way Jesus uses two distinct methods to communicate the truth he wants to get over. In the first half, Jesus talks about signs Matthew 24:4-35. In the second half Jesus talks in Parables.

It is important that we understand why Jesus may have done this. The Signs that Jesus refers to are describing what God will be doing before the return of Jesus. The parables, however, tell us what we should be doing, or how we should be living with his return in mind. Therefore, can I suggest that is probably more important that we understand and grasp the message behind the parables, and worry less about the signs, which we have no control over?

Before we look at the parable of the ten virgins we need to say a word about how we should read these parables. Parables are stories Jesus used to make a spiritual point. However, some people have fallen into the trap of how they interpret the parable; they believe that everything in the story has a secondary meaning. So these people think that the five foolish bridesmaids, the five wise bridesmaids, the lamps, the oil and the bridegroom are all allegories of something else. This kind of interpretation can cause confusion, robbing us of the truth that Jesus wants to communicate.

The Background of the Parable

A wedding was the greatest event in a village or a town. It was the greatest single social celebration; where everybody got involved, friends, family, extended family, everyone. It was a time of great happiness; it was a time of festivity and celebration. And that's the scene we have here.

But it's essential for us to know that in a Jewish marriage, there were three elements:-

The first is engagement.

Long before the scene we have here, there was an engagement. This was an official contract between the two fathers who were giving their daughter and their son to each other, as it were. So engagements weren't really made with the couple, they were made between the fathers.

The Second was the betrothal.

A little while after that, there would be what was called the second phase of the wedding or the marriage which was the betrothal. Now the betrothal was the official ceremony. The couple would come together before friends and family and they would make vows and covenants and binding promises. They had an actual marriage ceremony and they made their commitments. Then later they were then officially married. Any breaking of a betrothal period was only through a divorce. There had to be an actual divorce to dissolve the betrothal, this divorce was binding. Also if the husband happened to die during that period, the wife was considered a widow even though the marriage had not been physically consummated nor were they living together.

The third phase was the wedding feast.

This was when the groom would go to the bride’s house where she would be waiting with all of her bridesmaids. He would arrive with all of the men that are with him and he would collect his bride and her maids and they all go with torches, parading in the night through the village in a celebration of singing and joy that is unequalled in their social life. The day has finally come, everything is ready. He has prepared a home for her and is now going to get her and take her to that place. When they arrive at his home that night, the wedding party would go into the house and celebrate for as long as seven days. This starts at night time because they want to be able to go through the village with their lanterns so everyone would see them and enjoy the festival atmosphere.
prayer: Father thank you we can joyfully look forward to the return of Jesus.
